title: Tensor--Hom transposition and signed realization data
statement:
Use the coefficient stages, finite-Tor constructible categories $C(T,s)$, exceptional adjoint operations $F\dashv G$, and their inclusions and scalar conventions of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. A tensor--Hom transposition model for $F:C(X,s)\to C(Y,s)$ consists of Hom bifunctors $H_X,H_Y$ with closed structures [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], an ordinary adjunction $P\dashv Q$, and natural projection isomorphisms $F(PL\otimes M)\cong L\otimes FM$. Define the two bifunctors $A(M,N)=QH_X(M,GN)$ and $B(M,N)=H_Y(FM,N)$. Define the inverse exchange component $B(M,N)\to A(M,N)$ by applying, to the identity of $B(M,N)$, the five transpositions: inverse closed transpose on $Y$, precomposition by the displayed projection, $F\dashv G$, closed transpose on $X$, and $P\dashv Q$. A conclusion datum is an isomorphism $A\cong B$ whose inverse components are these arrows, with both Hom-variable shift structures, a shift structure on $Q$, and commutation of the isomorphism with integer shifts [def-weil-triangulated-category]. This is a type of data, not an assertion that such data exists.

At a finite or integral ring stage, a ring realization identifies these Hom and tensor structures, evaluation, $P,Q$ and their adjunction with the actual pro-etale operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and ringed-site duality models [def-zl-ringed-site-duality-model], using their signed evaluation. Projection realization identifies the chosen projection with the inverse of the actual proper/open compactification projection of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data], conjugated by the two fixed Koszul braidings and the tensor/pullback realization comparisons; it retains the K-flat tensor representative models [def-sfb-proetale-tensor-model]. Ring-shift realization pins the first Hom variable to the signed Hom-complex model, the second to the ambient target-Hom comparison, and $Q$ to its actual direct-image shift, with the ambient inclusions and signed models of [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data]. For an inclusion of a partial closed domain, partial realization means pair-domain preservation, Hom and tensor comparison isomorphisms, and equality of the resulting evaluation with the included partial evaluation [def-pod-partial-closed-interfaces]. Finally, for schemes and a separated finite-type map over the finite-field base with a chosen compactification [def-nagata-compactification], define stage admissibility as existence of invertibility of $\ell$ on the base and the corresponding finite, integral, rational, or algebraically closed exceptional-admissibility predicate [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]. None of these records asserts the tensor--adjunction theorem or its shift compatibility.
